notes: SIGKILL mid-turn, single top-level session -- mirrors claudecode's own 2-25 phase shape (session_birth/pid_bind/turn_start/process_exit, invariant 'no state_transition to error') but with a widened process_exit window versus claudecode's 20000ms, for the same reason: this scenario's own description states its daemon-side outcome is identical to muse's 1-2_session-end variant 3 (SIGKILL mid-turn), which this branch already recorded live (recordings/2026-09-14-05-59-39_irrlichd-0.6.3+e22b8c9/) and whose meta notes document a real, twice-reproduced race against #1962 (processlifecycle's kqueue watched map[int]string last-write-wins): every muse session launch also spawns a transient proc-<pid> presession watching the SAME OS pid, so the fast kqueue NOTE_EXIT callback can misattribute this session's own exit to that shadow instead. The redundant PIDManager.CheckPIDLiveness -> reapDeadOrInfraPID sweep (pid_manager.go:1095/1186, syscall.Kill probe keyed on each session's OWN persisted PID field, never on the shared kqueue map) recovers the correct session's process_exited within one sweep tick (5s base / 15s worst-case backoff) regardless of which path the fast kqueue callback took. process_exit is pinned with same_session_as to the real session specifically so an unpinned search cannot vacuously pass by matching the shadow's own (differently-timed) exit instead -- the same fix 1-2_session-end's spec needed after a live run proved the unpinned form matches the wrong session. Session-birth/pid-bind/process-exit timing bounds are carried over from claudecode's proven template and muse's own 1-2_session-end recording; record should tighten them once this specific cell has its own live capture. PRE-DRIVE SPEC FIX (#1960 record pass): pid_bind was originally relative_to "start" with no same_session_as, unpinned. This batch's own two prior cells (2-9, 2-22 recordings, same session) directly observed a genuine ~100-150ms race between the real session and its own transient proc-<PID> presession for who reaches 'ready'/gets pid_discovered first -- an unpinned phase can silently bind to the presession instead of the real session. Retargeted to relative_to session_birth + same_session_as session_birth, matching every other muse cell's pattern (2-14/2-22/2-23/2-9), before this cell's own first live drive rather than discovering it the hard way.
